result.summary:
ROOT CAUSE (independently reproduced against feature/WF03-ISS0442-20260904's real code via disposable git worktree at that branch's actual current tip, not re-quoted from ISS-0457.yaml): autofix_file/1 (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex:414-446) decides whether/how to fix a file by reading Map.get(Jason.decode!(raw), "status") -- Jason's own duplicate-key semantics, confirmed FIRST-key-wins by a fresh Mix.install([{:jason,"1.4.5"}]) probe against this branch's own mix.lock pin (Jason.decode!(~s({"status":"PASS","other":1,"status":"DONE"})) => %{"status"=>"PASS"}). splice_top_level_status/2 (same file, :501-541) rewrites via scan_for_status/4, whose `best` accumulator is unconditionally overwritten on every depth-1 `status` match (:538-540) -- genuinely LAST-match-wins by construction. On a duplicate-top-level-status document these two mechanisms therefore act on DIFFERENT occurrences. Demonstrated directly on a built fixture (handoffs/WF03-ISS0457-20260904/diagnosis/dup-status-fixture.json, full transcript in diagnosis/divergence-probe-transcript.txt): first occurrence "DONE" drives autofix_file/1's decision (fix needed, target "COMPLETED"), but the splice edits the LAST occurrence ("COMPLETE"->"COMPLETED") instead, leaving the FIRST occurrence -- the one actually reasoned about -- as the illegal, non-@legal_statuses value "DONE" in the output file, silently, while the tool reports {:fixed,"DONE","COMPLETED"} to its caller/stdout. No raise fires (the documented invariant-violation raise only triggers when zero depth-1 status keys are found, not this case) -- this is silent mis-repair, self-limiting only in that the next lint_handoffs run re-flags a fresh H1 violation on the untouched first occurrence.

FALSE-CLAIM RE-MEASUREMENT (independently re-derived, not inherited from ORCH's figure in ISS-0457.yaml): the branch's design doc AND the splice code's own comment (letflow.lint_handoffs.ex:487-491 on tip 73381fff) both assert the last-wins scanner 'mirrors Jason.decode/1's own last-key-wins semantics.' Confirmed FALSE by the same fresh probe above -- Jason 1.4.5 is first-key-wins, not last-key-wins, on this exact branch's own pinned version.

WHY EXISTING TESTS DIDN'T CATCH IT: they didn't need to catch a NEW regression -- TEST-DESIGNER already found and directly reproduced this exact discrepancy while building the ISS-0442 suite, documented it explicitly in a comment block at test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs:722-742 on the branch, and deliberately left it uncovered (rather than asserting the buggy behavior as correct) with a note flagging it for a follow-up issue -- which is the actual origin of ISS-0457 (discovered_by: TEST-DESIGNER, discovered_in_run: WF03-ISS0442-20260904). TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR and REVIEWER on that branch did not treat the gap as blocking. Confirmed NOT exploitable on real data: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's corpus scan (in ISS-0457.yaml) found zero duplicate-top-level-key handoffs across 1989 real files.

SEQUENCING RE-CHECK (re-derived live, not trusted from the dispatch, which described the branch as at 'Step 3 REVIEWER PASS ... next_action already routes to TEST-DESIGNER'): `git fetch origin feature/WF03-ISS0442-20260904` then `git log -1` shows the branch has since ADVANCED to commit 73381fff, 'Step 5 TEST-RUNNER -- PASS' (full suite 3202/3204, only known pre-existing rustc-toolchain-gap failures). `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/feature/WF03-ISS0442-20260904 origin/main` => NOT an ancestor: still genuinely unmerged. Per WF-03, the only steps remaining on that branch are Step 5's ISSUE-FIXER issue-close and Step Final (git merge) -- i.e. that branch is now one short step from landing, not mid-implementation as originally framed.

ROUTING VERDICT: FOLD INTO ISS-0442's OWN STILL-OPEN PIPELINE, as a REQUIRED item before that branch's Step Final merge -- do NOT defer to a separate post-merge CODE-DESIGNER dispatch. Reasoning: (1) The defective code (autofix_file/1's decode step, splice_top_level_status/2, and the false 'mirrors Jason.decode' comment/design-doc claim) exists ONLY on feature/WF03-ISS0442-20260904 and nowhere on main -- there is nothing on main yet for a separate follow-on branch to fix; a separate branch would have to re-diagnose the same not-yet-existing code, then merge-race against ISS-0442's own merge, then reconcile against whichever landed first. Folding avoids that entirely. (2) Direct precedent on this SAME run: REVIEWER already escalated an analogous gap (the depth==1-guard collision risk) from ADVISORY to a REQUIRED acceptance criterion for the next step, and it was closed out (commit 08caf1db, 'kill the depth==1-guard mutant + close remaining coverage gaps') before Step 5 passed -- the pipeline has already demonstrated it can absorb a REQUIRED fix-forward at this stage without re-running the whole workflow from scratch. (3) The branch is one step (Step 5 issue-close + Step Final merge) from landing; deferring would let a branch KNOWN to carry a false correctness claim and a real (if currently unexploited) occurrence-selection bug merge to main as-is, then require a second full WF-03 run (worktree diagnosis again, design, implement, review, test) to fix code that could instead be corrected in the branch that already owns full context on it. (4) Severity is genuinely MINOR/non-blocking-for-merge (0 real occurrences in 1989 files, self-limiting failure mode) so this is not an argument for blocking the merge outright -- but 'non-blocking for merge' and 'not worth fixing before merge, given the branch is still open and one step away' are different questions; the second one favors folding given how cheap the fix is expected to be (scan_for_status/4 needs a first-match-short-circuit, or a first-only variant of the scan, plus removing the false comment/design-doc claim either way) relative to the cost of a full separate WF-03 cycle.
